text:
emily: Heads-up — quick check before tomorrow's digest. Can we get a 3-min snapshot of momentum across launch posts + webinar signups? Mainly care about: conversion rate from post -> registration, top 3 referral sources, and any attribution weirdness.

jordan: I can pull a mini table in a sec. High-level: posts → regs conversion ~1.8% (last 7d), webinar CTR from posts 2.3%, top refs: linkedin, newsletter, paid-search.

emily: ok, can you break linkedin into organic vs sponsored? last time that was fuzzy.

jordan: sure. quick table:

```
Source           | Posts_Clicks | Registrations | Conv%
LinkedIn (org)   | 1,240        | 38            | 3.06%
LinkedIn (spon)  | 890          | 10            | 1.12%
Newsletter        | 420          | 12            | 2.86%
Paid Search       | 2,100        | 25            | 1.19%
Other             | 560          | 8             | 1.43%
```

jordan: LinkedIn organic is unusually high this week — might be 1 influencer repost or tag.

marta: FYI our attribution window for posts -> reg is 7d by default. Are we confident UTM tagging is consistent for the sponsored campaigns?

jordan: good call. I spot-checked the paid campaign utm_source=linkedin and utm_medium=cpc for the major ones. But there's a handful of older sponsored boosts using utm_campaign=boost_without_tags.

sam: that would undercount sponsored and overcount "organic" — saw that pattern in last quarter too. We should either unify campaign params or run a rule mapping known GCLID/ads click IDs to sponsored.

emily: can you propose a short remediation? we need one that can be executed before EOD so the digest numbers are stable.

sam: quick fix: apply a rule in GA/BigQuery that classifies referrals as sponsored if referrer domain matches linkedin.com AND landing page has param ad_id OR if click_timestamp aligns with ads_clicks table within ±10s. I'll attach a query.

marta: yes please share the SQL. Also, does the dashboard compute both last-7d and MTD for the same widgets? want both in the digest.

jordan: SQL snippet below (super-mini, run in BQ):

```
SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN REGEXP_CONTAINS(utm_campaign, r"boost_without_tags") THEN 'sponsored'
    WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM `project.ads_clicks` ac WHERE ac.gclid = hits.gclid AND ABS(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(hits.ts, ac.ts, SECOND)) < 10) THEN 'sponsored'
    WHEN REGEXP_CONTAINS(referrer, r"linkedin.com") AND NOT REGEXP_CONTAINS(utm_medium, r"cpc|paid|sponsored") THEN 'organic'
    ELSE 'other'
  END AS traffic_bucket,
  COUNTIF(event = 'post_click') AS clicks,
  COUNTIF(event = 'registration') AS regs
FROM `project.analytics.events` hits
WHERE event_date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 7 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE()
GROUP BY traffic_bucket
```

jordan: running now — will post numbers in 5m. :eyes:

ryan: quick note — I saw a small dip in newsletter opens yesterday after the A/B subject line test. That could ripple into reg numbers; flagging so we don't over-interpret LinkedIn lift.

emily: good catch. can product ops confirm cohort for the subject test so we can exclude it from the benchmarking window? @marta

marta: will check. If the test cohort is <15% traffic, we can exclude via user_property.test_group. I'll update the query if needed.

ops-bot: task created: #MARK-3421 "Run post->reg attribution fix + update digest" assigned to jordan, due 2025-10-03.

jordan: numbers back: after rule, linkedin sponsored regs = 9 (was 10), organic 37 (was 38) — small change but attribution cleaner. Overall conv remains ~1.8%. MTD panels updated.

emily: excellent. For digest: include the mini table + note that we applied the temporary mapping rule for sponsored boosts and we're rolling a permanent tag fix with paid team. Also call out newsletter test as caveat.

sam: will follow up with a short doc for paid ops on standardizing utm_campaign values.

emily: thanks all — if no one objects I’ll ship the digest at 10:30. :rocket:

jordan: :thumbsup:

marta: :+1:
